sub_unit_name: Boiler troubles: Sludges, Scales and Caustic embrittlement

content.title: Boiler Troubles
content.description: Boiler troubles are undesirable problems caused by impurities present in boiler feed water. The major boiler troubles are sludge formation, scale formation, and caustic embrittlement, which reduce boiler efficiency and may lead to equipment failure.

content.content: Boilers are widely used in industries to generate steam. Impure feed water leads to the deposition of dissolved salts and chemical reactions inside the boiler, resulting in sludges, scales, and caustic embrittlement. Proper water treatment helps prevent these problems.

content.title: Why Boiler Troubles Matter
content.content: Boiler troubles reduce heat transfer efficiency, increase fuel consumption, damage boiler components, and may even cause boiler explosions if not controlled.
Sludges are soft, loose, and non-adherent deposits formed by salts that are more soluble in hot water than in cold water. They generally accumulate in the colder parts of the boiler.

items.question: Reduced Heat Transfer
items.answer: Acts as an insulating layer, reducing heating efficiency.

items.question: Choking of Pipes
items.answer: Blocks water circulation and steam flow.

items.question: Fuel Wastage
items.answer: More fuel is required to produce the same amount of steam.

content.content: Scales are hard, adherent deposits formed on the inner surface of boilers due to the precipitation of sparingly soluble salts such as calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate.

content.title: Formation of Scales
content.description: Scale formation occurs due to the decomposition of bicarbonates and the decreased solubility of certain salts at high temperatures.

content.content:
Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃ + CO₂ + H₂O
CaSO₄ becomes less soluble at high temperatures and deposits as a hard scale.
Caustic embrittlement is the cracking of boiler metal due to the accumulation of highly concentrated sodium hydroxide (NaOH) at stressed portions of the boiler.

Na₂CO₃ + H₂O → 2NaOH + CO₂
The concentrated NaOH attacks boiler steel at stressed regions, causing intergranular cracks and weakening the boiler.

items.question: Sludge Control
items.answer: Use blow-down operation and proper feed water treatment.

items.question: Scale Prevention
items.answer: Use softened water and chemical conditioning methods.

items.question: Prevent Caustic Embrittlement
items.answer: Use phosphate conditioning, sodium sulfate treatment, and avoid excess NaOH concentration.

content.title: Industrial Importance
content.content: Proper boiler water treatment improves steam generation, reduces maintenance costs, extends boiler life, and ensures safe industrial operation.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Sludges are soft deposits formed by soluble salts.
Scales are hard deposits formed by sparingly soluble salts.
Scales reduce heat transfer and increase fuel consumption.
Caustic embrittlement is caused by concentrated NaOH attacking boiler steel.
Water treatment and chemical conditioning prevent boiler troubles.
